Class CopyMove

java.lang.Object
imageproof.CopyMove
public class CopyMove extends Object
Looks for copy-move candidates: two 16 x 16 blocks with exactly the same gray values.

Steps:

  1. Take blocks every 8 pixels over the whole image. Skip blocks that are flat (gray variance below MIN_VARIANCE, about 2 gray levels of standard deviation) or have almost no fine detail (3 x 3 residual variance below MIN_DETAIL), because smooth areas repeat by themselves. Noisy areas are kept, because noise makes each block unique.
  2. Give every kept block a hash of its pixels. Only blocks with the same hash are compared pixel by pixel. So the work grows with the number of blocks, not with its square. Pairs that are closer than two block sizes apart (32 pixels) in both directions are skipped, because nearby blocks are naturally similar.
  3. Group the matches by their shift (dx, dy). A copied object gives many matches with the same shift. Keep only groups with at least MIN_GROUP matches.

Limits keep the work bounded. When a limit is hit, truncated is set and coveragePercent() says how much of the block grid was searched.

Repeated patterns (tiles, bricks) also match, so a candidate is NOT proof of editing. No candidates does NOT mean the image is authentic. The search only finds copies moved by a multiple of 8 pixels, without rotation or scaling. It uses the gray values from Histogram and Noise.variance(int[][], Rectangle).
